title: Commissioning, the learning mechanics under test: a scripted factory that ignores its refusals, a scripted reflection (play it in a fork started with --learn scripted)
note: A test of the learning's mechanics, not a demonstration of learning (2026-09-29): both sides are scripts. The procedure factory's script does not understand its refusals and follows its written instructions: it sends a first step that stops the scrubber three times and its task ends STUCK. In a fork started with npm run fork -- run <id> --learn scripted, that end is the event: Mother reads the task's traces, the reflection's script writes the rule the factory kept breaking into its instructions (the fork's copy of specs/procedure/words.json), the station adopts it in the fork, and the factory, asked again, holds the floor from its first submission. What it proves is the chain (event, traces, pattern, proposal, guard, adoption in the fork, instructions read again); what a model learns is observed with the models, never scripted.

description: Asset: the CO2 scrubber of the Lab module of a lunar habitat, just installed and commissioned.
Purpose: keep the CO2 of the air the crew breathes within limits; its twin will be asked what if questions about scrubber speed strategies at night.

Physical components: the Lab module (a volume of air); the scrubber, variable speed, centralised: it serves Hab-B through the inter-module ventilation, which keeps running with the hatch closed (through the ducts alone; what it delivers as installed is not documented); a CO2 sensor in the Lab; a hatch between the Lab and Hab-B, closed during the test; a CO2 sensor in Hab-B; the crew (two operators in the Lab, two people in Hab-B).
Test just run: {test}, hatch closed. Apparent volume from the decay, one room assumed: {apparentVolume} m3 ({why}).
Objective: the twin must reproduce the CO2 of the Lab well enough to evaluate scrubber speed strategies.
